description: ignorePaths replaces config:recommended's list, since Renovate does not merge the option. So it is that list as Renovate 45.1.0's :ignoreModulesAndTests preset gives it, without **/test/**, and with test/acceptance and Go's testdata folders added. Without **/test/**, Renovate reads test/browser too, which holds no file a manager reads. test/acceptance/go.mod replaces github.com/divbast/ci with ../../.ci, the checkout just setup makes, which Renovate's clone lacks, so go mod tidy cannot run there, and Renovate leaves the module alone. It follows the root module instead: after each Go update of the root module, cmd/modsync gives it the root's version and go.sum lines of each module both require, as the rule below says. Go's testdata folders hold fixtures, which nothing builds or installs, such as the go.mod files cmd/modsync's tests read, so Renovate leaves them alone too.

packageRules.description: A Go module update edits go.mod and go.sum and nothing more unless go mod tidy runs too: go.sum then keeps lines only the old version needed, which go mod tidy -diff in just lint refuses, or lacks lines the new version needs, so go tool cannot build a tool from tools/go.mod. So Renovate runs go mod tidy in the directory of each go.mod it updates: the root module and tools/. It skips the tidy on a major update, which changes the module path in the imports too, and so needs a person.

test/acceptance follows the root module: after a Go update of the root module, and once go mod tidy has run, cmd/modsync gives test/acceptance the root's version, and the root go.sum's lines, of each module both require, and the PR commits test/acceptance's go.mod and go.sum with the update. It reads the two modules alone, with no network and no checkout of divbast/ci, and runs once for a branch however many updates it holds. A rule below that sets tasks of its own for the root module replaces these, since Renovate does not merge them, so it runs cmd/modsync too. Go is the release mise.toml pins, set here too, since a task's tools take their versions from these constraints and never from mise.toml.

templ's runtime, which go.mod requires, and its generator, which tools/go.mod runs, move in one PR: the generated code is written for the runtime of the same version, so a bump of either alone leaves the two apart. The PR runs the new generator once and commits the *_templ.go files it writes, so the pages are committed in step with it. These tasks replace the root module's cmd/modsync task, so they run cmd/modsync too, and commit test/acceptance's go.mod and go.sum. Go is the release mise.toml pins, set here too, since a task's tools take their versions from these constraints and never from mise.toml.

sqlc, which tools/go.mod runs, writes the query code under internal/store/storedb. A bump runs the new sqlc and commits only what it writes there, so the query code is committed in step with it. Go is the release mise.toml pins, set here too, since a task's tools take their versions from these constraints and never from mise.toml.

cmd/genicons writes internal/web/icons/icons.go from the icons lucide-static puts in node_modules, which Renovate's lockfile update never fills. A bump installs the locked packages, running no install script and no pnpmfile, then runs genicons, and commits icons.go alone, so the icons are committed in step with the package. Go and Node are the releases mise.toml pins, set here too, since a task's tools take their versions from these constraints and never from mise.toml; pnpm runs as the release packageManager names, which it switches to by itself.

pnpm is pinned in three places: mise.toml installs it, package.json's packageManager names it, and build/pnpm/package.json pins it for the Containerfile's Node stage. The three move in one PR, so the pnpm that installs locally, in CI and in the image build is the one Renovate updates the lockfile with.

Go as mise.toml installs it and as the constraints of the regeneration tasks above pin it, which Renovate updates as well, move in one PR, so the tasks run the Go that is used locally and in CI. The pins follow containerbase's build of each release, which comes hours or a day after Go's own, so the group opens only once it holds two updates or more: mise.toml's update alone waits for the pins.

Node as mise.toml installs it and as the lucide-static task's constraint pins it, which Renovate updates as well, move in one PR, so the task runs the Node that is used locally and in CI. The pin follows containerbase's build of each release, which comes hours or a day after Node's own, so the group opens only once it holds both updates: mise.toml's update alone waits for the pin.

Playwright and axe-core never merge by themselves. A new Playwright brings new builds of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, which can move pixels in the approved screenshot baselines, and a new axe-core can find what the last one did not, and no pull request's checks run the browser suite. So an update waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard, and once approved it does not automerge: a person runs just browser, has any new baselines approved, and merges it.
